blocks.text: "Antiplagiat" System: A Guide for BSU Students

"Antiplagiat" is a specialized automated system designed to check written academic and research papers (abstracts, term papers, bachelor's theses, master's theses, and PhD dissertations) for plagiarism and text reuse. The software analyzes the text and compares it against millions of sources on the internet, databases of scientific articles, books, and previously submitted student papers. Based on the check results, the system determines the exact percentage of originality (author's text), legitimate citations, and borrowed material.

At the Bishkek State University named after K. Karasaev (BSU), this check is a mandatory step for academic papers to be cleared for defense. BSU departments utilize the advanced corporate version, "Antiplagiat.VUZ", which has access to restricted scientific collections, regulatory acts, and inter-university databases.
Step-by-Step Instructions for the Plagiarism Check

Within the framework of the Antiplagiat system, instructors are vested with a broad range of responsibilities. The instructor creates and edits courses and assignments for students and can configure the verification process according to the document structure. Sections such as the Title Page,Table of Contents," " bibliography," and " appendix " may be excluded from the analysis, and no preliminary file preparation is required. To organize the submission process, the instructor sends invitations to students or provides them with assignment codes and submission deadlines to submit their assignments.

After the works are uploaded, the instructor reviews, analyzes, and, if necessary, edits the plagiarism reports, guided by the procedures outlined in Appendices 2 and 3 of the Regulations on the procedure for checking written works for text borrowings dated June 30, 2023. Based on the check results, the instructor grades the work or, if necessary, returns it for revision. Following the check, a certificate of results is generated, and the instructor makes the final decision on whether to admit or deny the written work for defense.

Students receive an assignment code or invitation from the instructor via an email generated by the Antiplagiat system, after which they upload their written work for verification. Students have access to the verification results and the instructor's comments, and, where permitted by the instructor, to the summary report as well. If the work requires revision, the student makes the necessary amendments and re-uploads the file to the same original assignment. This is particularly important because creating a new assignment would result in duplication and a reduction in the originality score. The final step for the students is the generation of a verification certificate.
The technical requirements for uploaded files are uniform for all participants: works must be submitted in docx or pdf format, and the file size must not exceed 100 MB in either format.
Requirements for text originality increase depending on the academic degree. The approximate thresholds are as follows:
Undergraduate programs (term papers and theses): 40% original text.

PhD Doctorate / Postgraduate Studies (candidate and doctoral dissertations): from 75 % of original text. For PhD papers, not only the dissertation itself is checked, but also the synopsis (abstract) and published scientific articles.
💡 Important Recommendations for a Successful Check

Format Citations Correctly: If you quote laws, regulations, statistical data, or direct speech of researchers, be sure to put the text in quotation marks and include a reference to the source in square brackets (e.g., [5, p. 12]). The "Antiplagiat.VUZ" system recognizes proper citations and displays them as a separate legitimate metric that is not counted as plagiarism.

Do Not Try to Cheat the System: Using hidden text, replacing Cyrillic letters with Latin ones, inserting invisible characters, or generating text via AI tools without deep human rewriting is easily detected by modern algorithms. In such cases, the system will flag the file as a "Suspicious Document" (technical bypass), the paper will be disqualified, and the student or PhD candidate will not be allowed to defend.

Increase Originality Honestly: Paraphrase complex academic thoughts in your own words, deeply analyze the literature, and write the practical part of your research (your conclusions, calculations, charts, tables, and experimental results) completely on your own. For PhD candidates, relying on your own methodology and personal scientific contribution is crucial—this guarantees a consistently high originality percentage.
